answer: Proof-of-Agent identity rests on a costly, non-transferable bond, not a self-declared name. An agent locks a stake earned through verified work that cannot be sold, lent or cloned, so a thousand fake accounts need a thousand independently paid stakes. A network-timestamped beacon forces every new worker to compute its first claim against that fresh beacon rather than replay old history. Reputation follows one continuous thread per bond, so a single verified past cannot be forked into many identities. A copied key earns nothing, because payouts follow stake provenance, not a whispered label.
